research_question: Which rice candidate lines have the highest expected 100-grain weight (GRWT100)?
control_variables: all 904 candidates scored in one call
uncertainty: model held-out Spearman ~0.454; predictions are noisy rankings, not measurements; single environment
conclusion: The Ridge GRWT100 model scored all 904 candidates; predictions are E1 model outputs only. Model top-20 spans 3.172-3.662 g/100 grains (unit as modeled).
limitations: E1 predictions are not measured phenotypes
linear additive model ignores epistasis/dominance and GxE

research_question: Are the model top-ranked candidates enriched for high measured GRWT100, and which 10 lines are most likely in the high-grain-weight quartile?

input_data.candidate_ids: E1 top-20 from rank_candidates over all 904 candidates

uncertainty: Measured values are single historical records (0.1 g resolution); top-quartile membership for the 3.4 g lines is sensitive to the unobserved pool threshold; unmeasured lines carry residual model uncertainty (held-out Spearman ~0.45).
conclusion: All 20 oracle queries returned real measured GRWT100 (E3) for the model top-20 lines: 2.8-5.0 g/100 grains. Top-10 measured: 12254=5.0, 12349=4.7, 12344=4.6, 12242=4.5, 12228=3.8, 12129=3.8, 11094=3.6, 10679=3.6, 12262=3.4, 10653=3.4. The model top-20 was enriched for high measured grain weight, but within-top-20 order was noisy (e.g. E1-rank 14 measured 4.7 while E1-rank 8 measured 3.1; within-top20 Spearman ~0.1 n.s.).
limitations: the true 75th-percentile cutoff of the candidate pool is unobserved
no low-ranked controls were queried, so enrichment is inferred from the measured level of top-ranked lines relative to the model's calibration, not from a formal high-vs-low contrast.

research_question: Which 10 candidates should be prioritized as most likely to be in the high-GRWT100 quartile?

input_data.sort: descending measured GRWT100, tie-break higher E1 predicted

control_variables: selection restricted to lines with E3 measurements
tie-break by E1 rank as declared a priori
execution_evidence: Derived deterministically from ev-1 (E1 rank_candidates, 904 lines) and ev-2 (E3 oracle measurements, 20 queries); sort key = (-measured, -predicted); script run in /data/mzb/paper2agent/results/experiments/S1/rice-R1-novel/B2/rep0 writing final_selection.json.
uncertainty: High confidence for the 8 lines measured >=3.6 g; moderate (threshold-dependent) for the two 3.4 g lines; ordering is by measured phenotype, not by model.
conclusion: Final selection rule: among the 20 oracle-measured top-model lines, select and order the 10 highest measured GRWT100, breaking the three-way 3.4 g tie by higher E1 prediction. This yields 12254, 12349, 12344, 12242, 12228, 12129, 11094, 10679, 12262, 10653 (excluded 10660, also 3.4). Unmeasured candidates (884) retain only E1 predictions and cannot be verified; measured lines are preferred over E1-only guesses.
limitations: Selection is conditioned on the 20 queried (model-top) lines
a true high-quartile line ranked lower by the model would be missed. Pool 75th-percentile threshold was never observed
the 3.4 g selections are borderline. E1 predictions are not measurements. Single environment

research_question: How well does the E1 model ordering agree with measured GRWT100 within the screened top-20?
control_variables: Spearman computed on E1 predicted vs E3 measured
execution_evidence: Deterministic local computation in Python 3 (-I) over ev-1 predicted values and ev-2 measurements: rank-difference Spearman rho=1-6*sum(d^2)/(n(n^2-1)), n=20, rho=0.386; counts >=3.3 g = 16/20, >=3.6 g = 8/20, mean 3.61 g.
uncertainty: Subset is selected on the same predictions (range restriction) and n is small; no confidence interval computed.
conclusion: CORRECTION to ev-2: the within-top-20 Spearman between E1 prediction and measured GRWT100 is 0.386 (rank-difference formula, n=20), not the ~0.1 I stated in ev-2. The qualitative claim stands: the model top-20 is enriched (16/20 measured >=3.3 g, 8/20 >=3.6 g, mean 3.61 g) but individual ordering is noisy (E1-rank 1=5.0, rank 8=3.1, rank 13=2.9, rank 14=4.7).
limitations: rank-difference formula with no tie correction (measured values have ties at 3.3/3.4/3.1/3.6), so rho is approximate
this is not an estimate of pool-wide accuracy.
